Terms of Reference

*This position is advertised under UNOPS ICA contractual arrangement*

In a fast-paced and complex operation, with a dynamic environment, the incumbent will be responsible to stay abreast of the challenges posed by the operational and political context in Bangladesh.

Working closely with the senior management and External Relations Unit, the incumbent will support the design and implementation of the external engagement strategy, and contribute to harmonization or outreach activities, in particular towards a wide range of stakeholders, partners and donors. He/she will assist the development, drafting and distribution of situation reports, briefing notes, background material, liaising with technical units, partners and key stakeholders to ensure qualitative content and timely dissemination. He/She will also support the Head of Office with meeting with external partners, elaborating talking points and ensuring efficient communication and information flow within the office, the operation and with key stakeholders of the Rohingya refugee response.

In the complex operating environment of Cox’s Bazar the incumbent will take the lead in planning, executing and reporting on key donor missions. These could be in-country ones (mainly organized through Embassies) but also from abroad: the latter include Government Ministers. MPs, Private Sector entities as well as UNHCR and UN Senior Officials.

In light of the above, strong interpersonal skills, organizational skills, strategic thinking, and excellent drafting and communicating in English is required. Solid experience in donor relations, communications, inter-agency coordination, logistics, and planning are essential, while a sense of humour is strongly desirable.

The incumbent may be required to supervise national affiliate personnel.. Thus, some managerial experience is required to be able to quickly delegate tasks within the team based on the assessment of the level/seniority of the mission.

The incumbent is expected to work on and assist in various external relations activities, including preparing communication materials for external audiences, donor reports or funding briefs. The incumbent will plan and organize activities to increase UNHCR’s outreach capacity, engage with a range of external stakeholders and entities to present UNHCR’s work and liaise with the government officials.

S/he should have demonstrated experiences working closely in the areas of external and donor relations, inter-agency coordination and government liaison. S/he needs to demonstrate the capability to work in a complex multi-functional environment, including inter-agency settings.

jobs.description:

Terms of Reference

This position is advertised under UNOPS ICA contractual arrangement.

General Background :

Although Bangladesh is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or the 1967 Protocol and the Government does not recognize the Rohingya as refugees, referring to them as “Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals”, the country is generously hosting some 1.2 million Rohingya refugees across 33 camps. This includes over 141,000 new arrivals who fled renewed violence and persecution in Myanmar’s Rakhine State and have entered the camps since 2024 despite the border being officially closure. The presence of large numbers of refugees – who now represent two-thirds of the local population in Cox’s Bazar – has had important impacts on local communities, service delivery, the economy and the environment. The Government considers return to Myanmar, as soon as possible, as the only viable solution. This policy approach impacts on the humanitarian operation, with the Government discouraging medium or longer-term approaches, including the development of permanent infrastructure, providing formal education or livelihoods opportunities for the refugees and the use of cash to deliver assistance.

With the escalation of the conflict in Northern Rakhine State since November 2023, the operation in Bangladesh has experienced the spill overs in the refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar. On the one hand, UNHCR and partners have been recording a significant increase in security incidents in the camps, including homicides and abductions. UNHCR has also seen an emerging trend of organised groups recruiting refugees to engage them in the armed conflict in Myanmar. The compromised civilian and humanitarian character of asylum in the camps has heightened risks for refugees, refugee volunteers (the backbone of the humanitarian response) and humanitarian workers. On the other hand, the operation has been recording new arrivals in the camps despite the Government’s closed-door policy at the border with Myanmar. New arrivals are extremely vulnerable, many have suffered injuries as they were fleeing. The government has authorized their assistance but without registration.

The Associate Protection Officer is part of the Legal Protection Unit (LPU) responsible for a broad portfolio of protection activities, including protection case management and response to complex and urgent protection cases; legal aid and access to justice, including legal counselling, assistance with filing complaints before police and courts, legal representation, and interventions to secure release from detention; camp and border protection monitoring; and protection coordination. Protection and border monitoring and analysis undertaken by the unit inform UNHCR's advocacy, including through weekly camp security monitoring updates and monthly border monitoring reports.

The unit maintains extensive engagement with law enforcement authorities and the judiciary, including through capacity development and support to the Government in upholding the civilian and humanitarian character of asylum and the camps and addressing the broader security situation in the camps. It also co-chairs the Anti-Trafficking Working Group with IOM.

The work of the LPU is a critical pillar of UNHCR Bangladesh’s protection strategy and advocacy, and close coordination with the Registration, Community-Based Protection, Durable Solutions and Field Units is required.

The complexity and fast-moving nature of the operation require an incumbent who is highly adaptable and solutions-oriented, able to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgement and deliver effectively under pressure.

In addition, the incumbent stays in close contact with government camp administration officials under the Office of the Refugee Repatriation and Relief Commissioner (RRRC). S/he also works closely with the Protection sector of Rohingya Coordination Platform (RCP). The incumbent will have supervisory responsibilities.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Essential:

  • Demonstrated experience on protection and border monitoring in sensitive contexts (access to asylum, refoulement, cross-border and onward movement), and protection advocacy;
  • Demonstrated experience on anti-trafficking and coordination in interagency context;
  • Demonstrated experience on civilian and humanitarian character of asylum and camps;
  • Demonstrated experience establishing excellent relationships with a variety of law enforcements authorities and the judiciary.

Desirable:

  • A Master’s degree in international refugee law or equivalent;
  • Excellent political awareness, ability to work independently and with minimal supervision, and demonstrated capacity to analyze complex and fast-changing operational contexts, including data;
  • Demonstrated experience protection teams and partner relationships;
  • Familiarity with and exposure to route-based approach;
  • Experience in the region and of the Rohingya Situation

Standard Job Description

Organizational Setting and Work Relationships

The Associate Protection Officer reports to the Protection Officer or the Senior Protection Officer. Depending on the size and structure of the Office, the incumbent may have supervisory responsibility for protection staff, including community-based protection registration, resettlement and education. S/he provides functional protection guidance to information management and programme staff on all protection/legal matters and accountabilities. These include: statelessness (in line with the campaign to End Statelessness by 2024), Global Compact on Refugees (GCR) commitments, age, gender, diversity (AGD) and accountability to affected populations (AAP) through community-based protection, Child protection, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention and response, gender equality, disability inclusion, youth empowerment, psycho-social support and PSEA, registration, asylum/refugee status determination, resettlement, local integration, voluntary repatriation, human rights standards integration, national legislation, judicial engagement, predictable and decisive engagement in situations of internal displacement and engagement in wider mixed movement and climate change/disaster-related displacement responses. S/he supervises protection standards, operational procedures and practices in protection delivery in line with international standards.

The Associate Protection Officer is expected to coordinate quality, timely and effective protection responses to the needs of forcibly displaced and stateless persons, ensuring that operational responses in all sectors mainstream protection methodologies and integrate protection safeguards. The incumbent contributes to the design of a comprehensive protection strategy and represents the organization externally on protection doctrine and policy as guided by the supervisor. S/he also ensures that forcibly displaced and stateless persons are meaningfully engaged in the decisions that affect them and support programme design and adaptations that are influenced by the concerns, priorities and capacities of forcibly displaced and stateless persons. To achieve this, the incumbent will need to build and maintain effective interfaces with communities of concern, authorities, protection and assistance partners as well as a broader network of stakeholders who can contribute to enhancing protection.

Duties

  • Stay abreast of political, social, economic and cultural developments that have an impact on the protection environment.
  • Promote International and National Law and applicable UN/UNHCR and IASC policy, standards and codes of conduct.
  • Foster their consistent and coherent interpretation and application through mainstreaming in all sectors and /or in clusters in applicable operations.
  • Assist in providing comments on existing and draft legislation related to forcibly displaced and stateless persons.
  • Provide legal advice and guidance on protection issues to forcibly displaced and stateless persons; liaise with competent authorities to ensure the issuance of personal and other relevant documentation.
  • Conduct eligibility and status determination for forcibly displaced and stateless persons in compliance with UNHCR procedural standards and international protection principles.
  • Promote and contribute to measures to identify, prevent and reduce statelessness.
  • Contribute to a country-level child protection plan as part of the protection strategy to ensure programmes use a child protection systems approach.
  • Contribute to a country-level education plan.
  • Implement and oversee Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all protection/solutions activities which integrate AGD sensitive procedures.
  • Oversee and manage individual protection cases, including those on GBV and child protection. Monitor, and intervene in cases of refoulement, expulsion and other protection incidents through working relations with governments and other partners.
  • Recommend durable solutions for the largest possible number of forcibly displaced and stateless persons through voluntary repatriation, local integration and where appropriate, resettlement.
  • Assess resettlement needs and apply priorities for the resettlement of individuals and groups of refugees and other forcibly displaced and stateless persons.
  • Participate in the organisation and implementation of participatory assessments and methodologies throughout the operations management cycle and promote AGD sensitive programming with implementing and operational partners.
  • Contribute to and facilitate a programme of results-based advocacy through a consultative process with sectorial and/or cluster partners.
  • Facilitate effective information management through the provision of disaggregated data on populations of concern and their problems.
  • Promote and integrate community-based approaches to protection and contribute to capacity-building initiatives for communities and individuals to assert their rights.
  • Support activities in the area of risk management related to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse, fraud, case-processing, data protection, and human rights due diligence at country level.
  • Participate in initiatives to capacitate national authorities, relevant institutions and NGOs to strengthen national protection related legislation and procedures.
  • Intervene with authorities on protection issues.
  • Negotiate locally on behalf of UNHCR.
  • Decide priorities for reception, interviewing and counselling for groups or individuals.
  • Enforce compliance of staff and implementing partners with global protection policies and standards of professional integrity in the delivery of protection services.
  • Enforce compliance with, and integrity of, all protection standard operating procedures.
  • Support the identification and management of risks and seek to seize opportunities impacting objectives in the area of responsibility. Ensure decision making in risk based in the functional area of work. Raise risks, issues and concerns to a supervisor or to relevant functional colleague(s).
  • Perform other related duties as required.

In some instances, the incumbent may be expected to work closely with the senior managers to liaise and coordinate with donor and government officials.

The incumbent is expected to work on and assist in various donor outreach, reporting and external relations activities, including preparing materials for external audiences, donor reports or funding briefs. The incumbent will plan and organize activities to increase UNHCR’s outreach and fundraising capacity, engage with a range of external stakeholders and entities to present UNHCR’s work.

The incumbent's primary role is pursuing opportunities for donor engagement, strengthening partnerships, sustaining support and fundraising opportunities. Due to the specific nature of these responsibilities, Donor Relations Officer posts are based only in Geneva Headquarters, major donor capitals or Regional Bureaux. S/he with also provide support to counterparts in Field Operations, especially to offices dealing with emergency situations.

The incumbent reports to a senior staff in the function of Donor Relations and/or External Engagement; the reporting relationships may vary and depends on the size and organizational structure of the office/operation. The incumbent may supervise professional and/or general service staff.

jobs.title: Technical Specialist, Water Sanitation and Hygiene Programme (WASH)
jobs.description:
Join BRAC’s WASH programme to be part of the vision to ensure that everyone, everywhere has safe drinking water, a hygienic toilet, and practices good hygiene.

We deliver services to people living in hard-to-reach, climate affected and underserved urban areas using a multidimensional approach - from financing WASH markets to building partnerships with local governments.

Active since 2006, the programme has significantly contributed to Bangladesh attaining the Millennium Development Goals national WASH target, and is believed to be the largest NGO-managed WASH programme in the world.

Working at brac is not like any other job. It is a platform where you can bring about real change for people who need it the most. We are not just dreaming of a better world, we are building it. Join us to find the way.

Job purpose

The Technical Specialist, WASH will be responsible to select the appropriate WASH technologies for communities/schools/industries/healthcare facility considering the geo-hydrological situation of the intervention areas; design the WASH facilities; support in preparing drawing and bill of quantity (BoQ), ensure the quality of installation of WASH facilities; organize and conduct training/orientation for stakeholders; follow-up/monitor the proper operations and maintenance (O&M) of the facilities; data collection on technical aspects and prepare periodical reports.

Key responsibilities

  • Prepare yearly/quarterly/monthly work plan for the identification, design and installation of WASH technologies for communities/schools/industries/healthcare facilities for the respective office in consultation with Manager Technical and other concerned staff.
  • Ensure smooth information flow and effective communication among relevant stakeholders and facilitate timely sharing of updates and resolution of any WASH-related issues
  • Participate in selection process of appropriate technologies and sites at communities/schools/industries/healthcare facilities considering the geo-hydrological situation, climatic condition and disaster of the intervention areas, gender and inclusion etc. as well as proper consultation with the user’s group.
  • Prepare detailed design of the selected technologies at communities/schools/industries/healthcare facilities considering the geo-hydrological situation and other important factors including the WASH programme/project guideline, Bangladesh building code, etc.
  • Support the Technical Officer/Associates/Assistant in preparing detailed drawing and BoQ with specification of each of the components of the WASH facilities and vetting those for finalization.
  • Assist the procurement team at local offices and Technical Officer/Associates/Assistant to procure quality materials by maintaining legal procedure of the organization and inspection of quality of each materials/services by the Technical Officer/Associates/Assistant.
  • Regularly monitoring & supervision the construction works for ensuring the quality of entire works, communicate with masons/workers and vendors according to field findings and recommend for any modifications or corrective measures.
  • Conduct field visit in regular basis for following up and monitoring the functioning of WASH facilities and discuss the findings with the users group at sites as well as document for sharing with the concerned colleagues of WASH programme.
  • Support the Technical Officer/Associates/Assistant to ensure the quality of water of the installed water supply technologies after the installation and before using by the user community, collecting water samples and testing with field kits as well as collection water samples properly and send it for laboratory test.
  • Prepare draft guideline/training module, organize and conduct training/orientation for entrepreneurs/Mason and Sinker groups etc. on proper installation/construction of WASH facilities (safely managed as per SDG criteria) and sustainable O&M for caretakers, WASH committees, etc.
  • Regularly collect technical information on WASH technologies, prepare periodic report (monthly, quarterly, annual, etc.) and share information with the concerned colleagues of WASH programme as well as keep the record of the project document and any other related documents.
  • Establish effective communication and coordination with different stakeholders at district/upazila level for collecting updated WASH information and sharing the information on BRAC WASH programme/project such as DPHE, LGED, LGIs (Union Parishad, Pourashava), WASH Entrepreneurs, Sinker group/Mason, Suppliers, WASH Committees, Forums, etc.
  • Ensure appropriate technical guidance for operation, maintenance and long-term functionality of WASH facilities.

Requirements

  • Education: Diploma
  • Experience: 4 years

Knowledge

  • Good knowledge of water and sanitation issues, and hygiene practice.
  • Good knowledge of Community mobilization and sanitizations and skills transfer.
  • Technical knowledge regarding water and sanitation options
  • Knowledge about civil, painting and plumbing work

Skills

  • Written and verbal communication skills both in Bengali and English
  • Computer Literacy (MS-Word, Excel, power point etc.)
  • Communication Skills

Competencies

Capacity building is achieved through climate-resilient adaptation of existing livelihoods, strengthening resilience against natural hazards, increasing agricultural productivity through modern technology, and diversifying income- generating activities. The purpose of the in-depth audit is to provide SoH with a sound basis for its accountability, transparency and accuracy in the financial disclosure towards the funding agency BMZ. The tasks of this recruitment relate to:

  • An annual audit, with a detailed examination of all the supporting documents for the period of 01.08.2026 – 31.12.2026;

This in-depth audit will verify the compliance with standards of the funding agency BMZ, SoH, national regulations and the international accounting standards (ISA).

The auditor will review all of the project’s financial documents, receipts lists, records of transactions, all vouchers and receipts disbursed, and relevant project documents in order to come up with a professional, independent opinion on the financial accounting of the project “Increasing resilience through climate change adaptation and sustainable livelihoods in Assasuni Upazila, Satkhira, Bangladesh” for all funds received and expended by BNM from 1st August 2026 to 31st December 2026.

Additionally, the audit shall give recommendations on strengths, weaknesses, and required improvement in the project-related financial and human resources management systems of BNM.

The audit will support the project quality assurance measures implemented by SoH and contribute to the decision-making process with regard to the project management and monitoring of finances by SoH and BNM.

Expected Deliverables

The auditor is expected to produce an audit report, an audit certificate and a management letter, which will comprise the following:

  1. Presentation of the scope and mandate of the audit, as well as the list of documents that formed the evidence for the audit,
  2. An opinion whether financial statements (statement of accounts broken down for each year being audited) are issued in accordance with the financial reporting framework of the project, BMZ requirements and an internationally recognized accounting standard,
  3. A checked, signed and stamped list of all (100%) project costs receipts, sorted by BMZ budget lines (list is provided by the local implementing partner).
  4. Recommendations on identified shortcomings, and, if applicable, comments on the follow-up of audit observations and recommendations from previous years.
  5. FD-4 Report according to Bangladeshi Law.

Audit documents can be issued in English or German.

The audit should focus on the following:

  • The correctness and completeness of the accounting records,
  • The financial report, showing all project related income and expenditure structured by budget lines,
  • Deviations of expenditure by budget lines. The expenditure, which exceeds or falls below the budget appropriations by more than 20 %, shall be explained separately, if the approval of the BMZ has not previously been obtained,
  • That receipts and relevant supporting documents are available for all project related income and expenditures (100% verification),
  • The management of the funds made available, which includes the transfer of project funds, all interest earned from the project funds during the reporting period and further income generated by the project,
  • Reviewing the appropriate use of funds according to the project objectives,
  • Evaluation of the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the usage of funds,

  • Reviewing if personnel costs and social security contributions conform to the regulations in the project country and are locally comparable,
  • The economical use of the project equipment and assets,
  • The inventory and the use of capital items, their whereabouts and their purposive usage,
  • Compliance with the legal framework of the project (project agreements and annexes, contracts, etc.) and the donor requirements,
  • Compliance with the policies of the local implementing partner regarding procurement, financial administration, human resources management and travel.

Procedures and Communication

The auditor will be given access to all necessary documents in the project offices through the local implementing partner BNM as well as relevant donor documents through SoH.

  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience conducting external independent audits of projects funded by international institutional donors in Bangladesh,

Companies as well as independent auditors are invited for this tender. Female and differently abled candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

jobs.description:
icddr,b is an international health research institute based in Bangladesh. Policymakers and practitioners utilise our evidence and expertise to improve health outcomes and prevent premature death and disability worldwide. In recognition of its scientific and humanitarian contributions, icddr,b has received numerous international and national awards, including

  • Gates Award for Global Health (2001): For its pioneering contributions to global health, including the development of oral rehydration therapy.
  • Independence Award (2005): For services rendered to the people of Bangladesh.
  • Conrad N. Hilton Humanitarian Prize (2017): For innovative approaches to addressing health challenges in underserved communities

Since its establishment in 1960, icddr,b’s research focus has expanded beyond cholera and diarrhoeal diseases to encompass a broad range of public-health challenges in Bangladesh and globally.

Our research priorities are organised around nine public-health goals:

  • Address health risks related to climate change;
  • Address health risks related to gender and sexual and reproductive health and rights;
  • Prevent and manage non-communicable diseases;
  • Improve healthcare in urban populations and achieve universal health coverage;
  • Prevent and control infectious diseases;
  • Improve maternal and newborn health;
  • Reduce maternal, adolescent and childhood malnutrition;
  • Enhance laboratory services and support genomics research; and
  • Improve hospital services and clinical research.

The Opportunity

We seek an accomplished, strategic and collaborative Director, Finance to provide leadership and oversight of icddr,b’s financial strategy, operations and governance.

Reporting directly to the Deputy Executive Director, the Director, Finance will lead a multidisciplinary finance team and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, Division Directors, Principal Investigators and donors to ensure sound financial stewardship and long-term organisational sustainability.

The successful candidate will combine strong professional expertise with integrity, sound judgement and inclusive leadership. The position will ensure effective financial planning, transparent reporting, robust internal controls and adherence to sound financial governance and applicable regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Planning and Development

  • Provide strategic leadership and overall direction for icddr,b’s Finance function, ensuring that financial strategy, resource allocation and financial management are aligned with icddr,b’s mission, research priorities and long-term institutional sustainability.
  • Serve as a trusted financial adviser to the Executive Director, Deputy Executive Director, Senior Leadership Team, Finance & Audit Committee (FAC) and Board of Trustees (BOT), providing independent advice and constructive challenge on financial performance, sustainability, funding, investment, risk and major institutional decisions.
  • Lead the development and implementation of icddr,b’s long-term financial strategy, multi-year financial plans, annual budgets, forecasts and scenario analyses, translating institutional and research priorities into sustainable financial plans and resource-allocation decisions.
  • Provide financial leadership on major research initiatives, institutional programmes, partnerships and funding opportunities, assessing their financial implications, affordability, risks and long-term sustainability.
  • Analyse funding patterns, expenditure trends and cost structures to inform strategic decisions and strengthen cost recovery.
  • Anticipate changes in the research, donor funding and operating environment and advise leadership on their implications for icddr,b’s financial resilience, funding model, cost structure and future resource requirements.

Financial Planning and Analysis

  • Lead the preparation of annual budgets, multi-year financial plans, cash-flow forecasts and scenario analyses.
  • Lead organisation-wide financial planning and performance management, ensuring effective alignment of resources with icddr,b’s research, programme and institutional priorities.
  • Establish consistent budgeting assumptions, guidelines and monitoring arrangements across the organisation.
  • Provide financial insight and constructive challenge to Division Directors, Principal Investigators and programme leadership to strengthen resource allocation, financial planning and organisational performance.
  • Establish appropriate financial performance measures and provide timely, forward-looking analysis of financial results, funding, expenditure, cost structures, cost recovery and resource utilisation to support management, FAC and BOT decision-making.
  • Hold overall accountability for the financial health, integrity and stewardship of icddr,b, ensuring that financial resources are managed effectively, transparently and in accordance with approved strategy and governance arrangements.

Financial Operations Management and Reporting

  • Oversee accounting, financial reporting, accounts payable and receivable, project finance and related financial operations.
  • Ensure that financial information and management reporting provide reliable, timely and decision-useful information for management and governance oversight.
  • Provide strategic leadership of icddr,b’s financial governance and control environment, ensuring appropriate policies, delegated authorities, accountability mechanisms and internal controls are established and operating effectively.
  • Ensure that accounting policies, financial reporting and practices remain aligned with applicable international standards, including IPSAS, as well as relevant laws, regulatory requirements, donor obligations and icddr,b policies.
  • Provide timely financial reports and analysis to the Deputy Executive Director, Executive Director, Division Directors, Board of Trustees and donors, in accordance with established reporting arrangements.
  • Promote efficient, responsive and service-oriented financial support across the organisation.

Financial Systems and Process Improvement

  • Lead the strategic evolution and modernisation of the Finance function, ensuring that its operating model, capabilities, systems and processes remain fit for icddr,b’s evolving research, funding and institutional environment.
  • Set the strategic direction for Finance systems, digitalisation, automation, data and management information, ensuring these enable effective financial management, strong controls and informed organisational decision-making.
  • Provide strategic oversight of icddr,b’s financial reporting framework and accounting architecture, including the effective application of IPSAS and adaptation to evolving accounting and reporting requirements.
  • Sponsor and oversee major Finance transformation and continuous-improvement initiatives, ensuring that investments in systems, processes and capabilities deliver sustainable improvements in efficiency, transparency, control and service quality.
  • Ensure that ERP and other financial systems provide integrated, reliable and decision-ready information across icddr,b and support effective financial governance and performance management.

Project Fund Management

  • Provide strategic oversight of grants, contracts and collaborative research agreements, working with Principal Investigators, Division Directors and programme leadership to ensure sound financial stewardship, appropriate cost allocation and recovery, effective financial management and compliance with donor and contractual requirements.
  • Support Principal Investigators and programme teams in proposal budgeting, expenditure planning, financial monitoring and project close-out.
  • Ensure appropriate cost allocation, indirect-cost recovery and compliance with donor-specific financial requirements.
  • Review and approve project budgets and financial transactions within delegated authority.
  • Ensure timely and accurate donor financial reporting and resolve escalated financial and contractual issues.
  • Promote constructive collaboration between Finance, research teams, donors and partner institutions.

Risk Management

  • Oversee material financial risks relating to research funding, institutional sustainability, liquidity, foreign exchange, investments, financial reporting, fraud, compliance and donor obligations, ensuring significant risks are identified, escalated and appropriately managed.
  • Maintain appropriate controls to prevent and detect fraud, misuse of funds and material financial misstatement.
  • Ensure effective segregation of duties and compliance with delegated financial authorities.
  • Oversee financial due diligence on relevant banking institutions, service providers and partners.
  • Promote financial accountability, ethical conduct and risk awareness across the organisation.

Audit and Compliance

  • Provide executive oversight of statutory, external and donor audits and work closely with Internal Oversight, while respecting its independence, to strengthen assurance and ensure timely resolution of material findings and agreed recommendations.
  • Support internal audit and assurance activities while respecting the independence of the Internal Oversight function.
  • Ensure timely implementation and monitoring of agreed audit recommendations.
  • Maintain effective relationships with auditors, donors and relevant regulatory authorities.
  • Maintain effective senior relationships with donors, auditors, regulators, financial institutions and other key external stakeholders on significant financial, contractual and regulatory matters.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable taxation, regulatory and contractual obligations.

Treasury Management

  • Oversee cash-flow forecasting, liquidity management, banking relationships and foreign-exchange exposure.
  • Oversee liquidity, reserves, investments and other institutional financial resources, ensuring an appropriate balance between financial resilience, risk, return and icddr,b’s strategic priorities.
  • Develop and review treasury and investment policies within approved governance arrangements.
  • Oversee the prudent management of surplus funds, reserves, endowments and separation funds.
  • Report regularly on liquidity, investment performance and treasury risks.

Leadership and Team Development

  • Lead and develop the Finance function through its management structure, establishing clear accountability and performance expectations across its respective units and ensuring effective integration and collaboration across the function.
  • Build a high-performing Finance leadership team with the professional capability, managerial strength and succession depth required to support icddr,b’s evolving strategic and operational needs.
  • Foster a culture of integrity, accountability, collaboration, service excellence and continuous improvement across Finance.
  • Position Finance as a strategic business partner to icddr,b’s scientific, research, programme and corporate leadership, providing insight, advice and constructive challenge to strengthen organisational performance, research delivery and financial sustainability.
  • Lead significant organisational change within Finance and ensure the function continuously develops its capabilities in response to changing technologies, accounting standards, funding models and institutional priorities.
  • Represent the Finance function at senior institutional and external forums and contribute to icddr,b-wide strategy, performance, risk and institutional decisions.

Qualifications and Experience:

Essential Requirements

  • A master’s degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
  • At least 15 years of progressively responsible experience in accounting, finance or financial management, including at least five years in a senior financial leadership role with substantial responsibility for financial strategy, operations, governance and team management.
  • Fellowship of a recognised professional accountancy body, FCA, FCCA, FCMA, FCPA is mandatory. Candidates must hold at least one of these designations and maintain current membership in good standing with the awarding professional body.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-million-dollar budgets and multiple funding sources in an international, donor-funded or comparably complex organisation.
  • Substantial experience in financial planning and analysis, accounting, management reporting, treasury, audit, internal controls and financial risk management.
  • Demonstrated experience in grant and contract financial management, including donor compliance, cost recovery and financial reporting.
  • Strong working knowledge of internationally recognised accounting standards, including IPSAS and/or IFRS.
  • Proven experience leading financial process improvement, organisational change and the implementation or optimisation of ERP systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to advise executive leadership and communicate financial performance, risks and recommendations to governing bodies or equivalent senior decision-makers.
  • Proven ability to lead and develop diverse teams and collaborate effectively with financial and non-financial stakeholders.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.

Desirable Requirements

  • Experience in an international health research institution, university, development organisation, public-health organisation or other not-for-profit institution.
  • Formal training or certification in IPSAS and practical experience implementing or transitioning to an international accounting framework.
  • Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, Oracle Financials or a comparable ERP platform.
  • Experience managing endowments, institutional reserves and investment portfolios.
  • Knowledge of Bangladesh’s financial, taxation and regulatory environment.
  • Experience working across multiple countries, cultures or regulatory environments.

Key Skills

  • Analytical rigour – translates complex financial data into clear, actionable insight for financial and non-financial audiences alike;
  • Sound, independent judgement – comfortable making high-stakes financial calls under time pressure or incomplete information;
  • Integrity under scrutiny – upholds rigorous controls and ethical standards even under programme or donor pressure;
  • Systems thinking – understands how financial decisions ripple across research operations, HR, IT and institutional risk;
  • Cross-functional communication – builds trust and negotiates effectively with donors, auditors, regulators, scientists and field teams alike;
  • Change leadership – drives adoption of new systems and processes (e.g. ERP, IPSAS) with genuine staff buy-in rather than top-down mandate;
  • Coaching and talent development – builds bench strength and succession within the finance function itself;
  • Resilience under resource constraint – sustains service quality and team morale through funding volatility or donor-driven change;
  • Diplomatic acumen – navigates competing priorities between the Board, donors and scientific leadership without compromising financial discipline; and
  • Hands-on digital fluency – works directly and confidently with financial systems, dashboards and data-analytics tools, not just through others.

Compensation

This internationally recruited position offers a competitive salary paid in US Dollars.

The successful candidate will receive an initial three-year contract, including a one-year probationary period. Contract renewal will be subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability.

How to apply

Application Process

Interested candidates are invited to submit a detailed curriculum vitae and cover letter, outlining how their qualifications and experience meet the requirements of the position, to the Director, Human Resources, at directorhr@icddrb.org

Please mention "Director, Finance" in the email subject line.

Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

icddr,b is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Qualified candidates from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Applications from women are particularly encouraged. For further information about the organisation, please visit www.icddrb.org.
